prompt:
Image 1 is a grey clay maquette of this figure: follow its pose, its parts and its framing, the whole figure from head to foot filling the square as it does, seen three-quarter front from a little above. It is a crude blockout: take its pose, its parts and its framing, not its stubby proportions. Paint over it completely: no grey clay and no plain smooth shapes may remain. Image 2 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 2.

A full-length painted portrait of the Oracle of the Flux, a god who sees the shifting currents of magic: a tall, slender, robed seer-god, larger than a man, floating a hand's breadth above the ground, in a regal pose: upright and still, head level, the staff held upright in its right hand, the left hand open at its side. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the cowl about 6% from the top edge and the floating hem about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the cowl, the shoulders and the staff that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the floating hem.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the cowl, the staff and the floating robe against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the figure is its robe and cowl: dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. All metal is dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn. Nothing in the image glows: the orb is dark smoky glass and the glyphs are thread. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Headgear: a deep cowl of the robe's cloth drawn forward so that it shadows the face; the lower face shows: ash-grey skin (#8F8C88), a thin calm mouth, a narrow chin; the eyes are lost in the cowl's shadow. Body: a long, flowing robe of dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour that covers the body from the shoulders to below the feet, with no mantle and no cape; runic glyphs embroidered in lichen grey-green (#909080) thread in a band down the front and around the hem; slender ash-grey hands. The floating hem: the robe does not touch the ground; its hem drifts and frays into soft, ragged trailing wisps of cloth a hand above the ground, and no feet show. Staff: a tall straight staff of dark wood whose head is a cage of dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn bands holding a smoky dark glass orb. Proportions: tall and heroic, a towering figure with long legs (the legs about half of its height) and the head about one eighth of its height; never squat, stocky, short-legged or dwarf-like.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view.
